calls.summary: Marcus Whitfield, CFO at a regional health system, called about outsourcing denials management and appeals for his hospital group. Oscar walked him through root-cause analysis and prevention workflows, then scheduled a consultation with a revenue cycle specialist. Marcus was impressed and confirmed the meeting.

Dana Alvarez, VP of value-based care at a physician group, asked about population health and care coordination services. Lila explained risk stratification and quality-measure reporting, then booked a consultation to review PMPM pricing. Dana was enthusiastic about the fit.

Gregory Sun, revenue cycle director, called to check the status of a medical coding compliance audit report that was in progress. Rosey confirmed the DRG validation was on track and shared the delivery timeline. Gregory was satisfied with the update.

Priya Nair, controller at a newly acquired hospital, called to schedule an end-to-end revenue cycle management consultation. Lee collected her contact details, net patient revenue figures, and current pain points, then booked the consultation with an RCM advisor. Priya appreciated the thorough intake.

Thomas Reed, practice manager, wanted a quote for insurance eligibility and benefit verification services. Mary explained per-transaction pricing and real-time payer checks, then scheduled a consultation. Thomas agreed to move forward.

Karen Boyle, patient financial services lead, disputed a billing invoice for patient collections that seemed higher than her contracted percentage. Sue reviewed the account and opened a billing adjustment case. Karen remained cautious but calmer by the end.

Nathan Cole, HIM manager, called about outsourcing medical coding for a backlog of facility charts. Mike outlined per-chart pricing and turnaround, then booked a consultation with a coding lead. Nathan scheduled the meeting.

Angela Ruiz, IT director, reported an integration issue with the eligibility verification feed after a recent system update. Jennifer logged the technical ticket and escalated to the implementation team. Angela wanted a faster resolution.

Daniel Pope, CFO, called to cancel a charge description master management engagement, citing budget cuts. Rose confirmed the cancellation terms and documented the request. Daniel was firm but civil throughout the call.

Sofia Grant, quality director, inquired about clinical documentation improvement services and physician query workflows. Oscar described concurrent chart review and scheduled a consultation. Sofia booked the follow-up.

Brian Kelly, billing supervisor, complained that denials management appeals were taking too long and hurting cash flow. Lila apologized, reviewed the account, and opened an escalation. Brian stayed frustrated by the end.

Melissa Ford, controller, disputed a billing statement for third-party collections fees she did not recognize. Mary pulled the contract and promised a written breakdown. Melissa was unhappy about the delay.

Victor Hale, revenue cycle VP, called angry about a spike in claim denials since onboarding. Lee acknowledged the denials trend and escalated to the account manager. Victor demanded a callback within 24 hours.

An unidentified caller from a physician practice left a voicemail asking about population health management pricing but did not leave a callback number. The message rolled to voicemail after hours. No agent was available to assist.

Rachel Simmons, office manager, called to complain about repeated errors in patient statements and poor communication from her assigned team. Sue apologized and logged a formal complaint for review. Rachel threatened to end the contract.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes. The caller represents a new independent urgent care clinic group expanding from single to three locations. They are looking for revenue cycle management services to handle patient eligibility verification, insurance benefit checks, and billing operations as they scale.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects a consultation with a specialist to review Conifer's patient access solutions and end-to-end RCM capabilities. They need to understand pricing and timeline for implementation before opening the additional two locations in Q1.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: Marcus should have captured the caller's email address for scheduling confirmation and sent a pre-consultation questionnaire. Asking about current claim denial rates and patient collections performance would have better qualified the opportunity and tailored the specialist's approach.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Conifer Health Solutions. This is Marcus Bell. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. My name is Sarah Chen. I'm the operations manager at Premier Urgent Care Group. We're currently operating one location in Austin, and we're opening two more clinics in the Dallas area within the next few months. We need help with our patient billing and insurance verification.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks Sarah. Premier Urgent Care sounds like a great fit for what we do. Just to confirm, you're looking for revenue cycle management services to support your patient access and billing operations as you expand?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Exactly. We're handling most of that internally right now, but it's becoming a bottleneck. We need professionals who can verify insurance benefits quickly and manage our billing workflow efficiently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I completely understand. That's where Conifer can really add value. Before I connect you with a specialist, let me grab a few quick details. You mentioned one location in Austin and two planned locations in Dallas. Are all three locations in Texas?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, all in Texas. Austin headquarters, then the new clinics in the Dallas suburbs, probably Frisco and Plano areas. We're also planning to add one more location in Houston by mid-year.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. Four locations total, all Texas. That's helpful context. And Sarah, can I capture your best contact number for our scheduling team?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure, it's ****, please keep that on file.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, I've got that. One more thing for our records. What's the best email address to reach you at, Sarah?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Oh, just send anything to the general clinic line for now. I'm juggling a lot this week. Marcus, when do you think someone could meet with us?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I appreciate that. Our consultants typically have availability within 3 to 5 business days. Let me see what we can schedule. Are mornings or afternoons better for your team?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Mornings work best for us. Ideally next Tuesday or Wednesday if you have something.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. I'll have our revenue cycle specialist reach out to you by end of day tomorrow to confirm a time slot for next Tuesday or Wednesday morning. Sarah, is there anything else I can help clarify before we wrap up?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, that sounds perfect. Thanks Marcus.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing Conifer Health Solutions. We look forward to meeting with you soon. Have a great day, Sarah.

callDetail.aiSummary: Sarah Chen from Premier Urgent Care Group, an independent three-location urgent care operator in Texas, called to inquire about Conifer's patient access and revenue cycle management services. The clinic is expanding from one Austin location to additional sites in Dallas and Houston and needs professional support for insurance benefit verification and billing operations. Marcus gathered key location and service information, confirmed the consultation need, and scheduled a follow-up appointment with a revenue cycle specialist for next week. The call was well structured with proper greeting and close, though email contact information was not fully captured for direct scheduling confirmation.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, great job structuring this call and moving Sarah toward a consultation efficiently. Your confirmation questions were clear and kept the momentum going. Two quick coaching notes for next time. One, when a prospect gives you hesitation on email, gently push back and get it anyway. A direct email helps the specialist personalize the pre-call questionnaire and increases show-up rate. Two, it would have been valuable to ask Sarah one quick qualifier like their current monthly patient volume or claims count so the specialist can arrive more prepared and better estimate the value of our solutions. Otherwise, smooth handling.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Conifer Health Solutions, this is Marcus. How can I help your organization today?
highlights: Thank you for calling Conifer Health Solutions

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. My name is Diane Whitfield, I'm the VP of Revenue Cycle at a regional health system. We're getting hammered on claim denials and I wanted to understand what you all offer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks Diane, and I appreciate you reaching out. Can you tell me a little about the size of the system and where you're seeing the most pressure?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We're four hospitals, roughly nine hundred beds combined. Our initial denial rate is sitting around twelve percent and our A/R days keep climbing. It's getting hard to manage.
highlights: initial denial rate is sitting around twelve percent

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's exactly the kind of problem our Denials Management and Appeals service is built for. We do root-cause analysis, handle the appeals, and put prevention workflows upstream so the same denials stop recurring.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay. And is that something you can do on its own, or do we have to hand over the whole revenue cycle to you?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Either way works. Many clients start with focused Denials Management, and some move to our End-to-End Revenue Cycle Management once they see the recovery. We can also layer in Clinical Documentation Improvement, since weak documentation drives a lot of denials.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That CDI piece is interesting, honestly our documentation is part of the problem too. But before we go further, what does denials management typically run? I need to keep this manageable for my board.
highlights: what does denials management typically run

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Completely fair. Denials work is usually priced as a percentage of the dollars we actually recover for you, generally in the four to eight percent range, so it scales with results rather than a big fixed cost. CDI is typically an annual engagement per hospital.
highlights: percentage of the dollars we actually recover

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's reasonable. I'll be honest though, we're also talking to another vendor we've used for coding, and they're pitching us on the same thing. I'm getting a couple of proposals side by side.
highlights: getting a couple of proposals side by side

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That makes good sense, and I'd encourage you to compare closely. Where Conifer tends to stand apart is scale and the AI-driven prevention, we manage twenty five billion in net patient revenue annually, so our denial pattern data catches issues before claims go out.
highlights: twenty five billion in net patient revenue annually

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's a strong point. One thing though, I don't want to get locked into some long multi-year commitment before we've seen it work.
highlights: don't want to get locked into some long multi-year commitment

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Understood, and we can structure an initial scoped engagement so you can validate the recovery lift first. The best next step is a consultation where our revenue cycle team reviews your denial data and shows projected impact. Could I get that scheduled for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, let's do that. I'll need to loop in our CFO as well, he'll want to be on the call.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, we'll include him. I have Thursday at 10 AM open. I'll send the invite to you and your CFO. What's the best email for you, Diane?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: It's d.whitfield at the health system, I'll reply with my CFO's address.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful, you're booked for Thursday at 10 AM and I'll get that invite out today. Thank you for calling Conifer, Diane, we look forward to helping you recover more, faster.

transcript.text: Hi there. This is Sarah from Conifer Health Solutions. We help hospitals and health systems optimize their revenue cycle and reduce claim denials. Do you have a few minutes to chat?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah sure. I'm the billing director at a mid-size hospital in Colorado. We're drowning in denials right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I hear that often. Denials are one of the biggest revenue leaks. Can you tell me roughly how much revenue you're losing to denials each quarter?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Probably around 3 to 5 million per quarter. It's frustrating because we don't have the staff to handle all the appeals.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a significant amount. With the right denials management and appeals process, we typically help clients recover 60 to 75 percent of that. Are you currently outsourcing any of your RCM work?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No we're handling it all in house but clearly that's not working. What does your service cost?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Our denials management service runs about 4 to 8 percent of recovered dollars, so you only pay when we recover money. Plus we can handle your appeals workflow. Would a consultation with our RCM specialist make sense this week?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah that would be helpful. When could we set something up?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great. How about Thursday the 13th at 2 PM Mountain Time? I'll send you a calendar invite and our specialist will walk through your denial trends.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Thursday at 2 works for me. What's the number to call if I need to reschedule?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. You'll get a reminder tomorrow. If you need to reschedule call us at 877-936-2933. We're looking forward to showing you how we can improve your cash flow.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Thanks Sarah. See you Thursday.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks so much. Have a great day.

qaPairs.question: What does Tenet Business Services actually do?
qaPairs.answer: Through Conifer Health Solutions we provide end-to-end revenue cycle management, clinical revenue integrity, accounts receivable management, and value-based care services for healthcare organizations. I can book a consultation to map these to your needs.

qaPairs.question: What types of organizations do you work with?
qaPairs.answer: We serve hospitals, health systems, physician practices, employers, and health plans. Let's schedule a consultation so a specialist can tailor a plan to your organization.

qaPairs.question: How much does revenue cycle management cost?
qaPairs.answer: Pricing is contract-negotiated and depends on your volumes and the services you need, so I can't quote an exact figure over text. A specialist can build a precise proposal during your consultation.

qaPairs.question: Can you handle our entire revenue cycle?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our end-to-end model covers patient access, coding, billing, accounts receivable, and denials under one agreement. I'd recommend a consultation to scope the full engagement.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer denials management?
qaPairs.answer: We provide denial root-cause analysis, appeals, and prevention workflows to help recover and protect revenue. Let's set up a consultation to review your current denial rates.

qaPairs.question: Can you help reduce our claim denials?
qaPairs.answer: Our teams identify denial drivers and build prevention workflows to lower future denials while appealing existing ones. A specialist can quantify the opportunity in a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you provide medical coding services?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer professional and facility coding, compliance audits, and DRG validation. I can book a consultation to discuss your coding volumes and goals.

qaPairs.question: What is clinical documentation improvement?
qaPairs.answer: CDI includes concurrent chart review, physician queries, and documentation accuracy work that supports appropriate reimbursement. Let's schedule a consultation to see how it fits your facility.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer patient access and eligibility verification?
qaPairs.answer: We handle insurance and benefit verification, pre-certification, registration, and financial clearance. A consultation is the best way to align these with your front-end workflows.

qaPairs.question: Can you support value-based care and population health?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we provide care coordination, risk stratification, and quality-measure reporting for value-based programs. I can arrange a consultation with a population health specialist.

qaPairs.question: How do you handle patient collections and communications?
qaPairs.answer: We manage self-pay outreach, statements, and contact-center support to improve collections while protecting the patient experience. Let's book a consultation to review your patient balance profile.

qaPairs.question: Do you work with physician group practices?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer group-practice billing, credentialing support, and denials management. A consultation will let a specialist scope your practice's needs.

qaPairs.question: Can you integrate with our current EHR and systems?
qaPairs.answer: Our teams work across major health IT platforms and tailor integration to your environment. A specialist can confirm the technical details during your consultation.

qaPairs.question: How long does implementation take?
qaPairs.answer: Timelines vary by scope and volumes, so we set a realistic go-live plan during onboarding. Let's book a consultation to outline a schedule for your organization.

qaPairs.question: Do you use AI and automation?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we are actively investing in AI and automation to accelerate cash and reduce manual work across the revenue cycle. I can schedule a consultation to show how it applies to you.

qaPairs.question: What kind of reporting will we get?
qaPairs.answer: You get analytics dashboards for KPI monitoring, cash-flow, and yield performance. A consultation will let us tailor the reporting to your leadership team.

qaPairs.question: Can you provide references or case studies?
qaPairs.answer: We support large health systems and can share relevant case examples during your evaluation. Let's set up a consultation to review results similar to your organization.

qaPairs.question: How do we get started?
qaPairs.answer: The first step is a consultation with a revenue cycle specialist to understand your volumes and goals. I can propose a day and time right now.

qaPairs.question: Do you serve organizations nationwide?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we support clients across the United States. Share your location and I'll book a consultation with the right specialist.

qaPairs.question: Can we outsource just one part of our revenue cycle?
qaPairs.answer: Absolutely, we offer focused point solutions as well as end-to-end services. A consultation will help us scope the specific area you want to address.
